function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is any vpn is installed". They want to know if any VPN is installed. We need to check if any VPN is installed. We can use the cmd_controller_execute tool to run a command that checks for installed VPNs. On Windows, we can query installed programs via WMIC or PowerShell. For example, we can run:

powershell "Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'VPN' } | Select-Object Name"

But we might want to list all installed programs and filter for VPN. Or we can use wmic product get name.

We can run a command that lists installed programs and then parse output. But the tool only returns raw output. We can run a command that prints the names of installed VPNs. For example:

powershell "Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'VPN' } | Format-Table Name"

But we might want to capture output. The tool returns output. We can then parse it. But we can also just run a command that prints the names. Let's do:

powershell "Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'VPN' } | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name"

This will print each name on a new line. Then we can parse. Let's do that.
